newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-CELTICS ELECT NOT TO PROCEED WITH RADJA DISPUTE.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-CELTICS ELECT NOT TO PROCEED WITH RADJA DISPUTE.

text.p: The Boston Celtics have decided not to pursue their appeal over the Dino Radja trade with the Philadelphia 76ers, apparently clearing the way for an eight-player trade between the 76ers and New Jersey Nets.

The Celtics traded Radja to the Sixers last Friday for forward Clarence Weatherspoon and centre Michael Cage but Radja, who didn't want to join the Sixers, balked at reporting, then failed a physical Tuesday. Philadelphia then declared the trade null and void.

But the Celtics, believing that Radja was healthy enough to pass the physical, asked the NBA to settle the matter. The NBA was to hold a hearing Friday in New York but the Boston club threw in the towel Thursday.
"We will not contest Philadelphia's decision not to proceed with the trade for Dino Radja," the Celtics said in a statement.

"We believe Philadelphia negotiated in good faith and they have now expressed doubts about Radja's physical condition. We plan to continue Dino's rehabilitation programme and will continue to explore all avenues to benefit the Boston Celtics."
This apparently clears the way for the deal -- widely reported but unconfirmed -- between the Nets and 76ers.

Under Wednesday's draft-day deal, the 76ers would send forward Keith Van Horn, the second overall pick in the draft, guard Lucious Harris forward Don MacLean and a player to be named -- most likely Cage -- to the Nets.
The 76ers would receive guard Jim Jackson and centre Eric Montross and two picks from the draft -- forward Tim Thomas, the seventh overall pick, and guard Anthony Parker, the 21st overall selection.
But since Cage was a part of the Radja trade, he could not be traded again until the NBA ruled on the Celtics-Sixers deal -- nor could the teams talk about it.
"We were told very sternly not to make any comment," said Nets coach John Calipari.

The 6-11 (2.11 metres) Radja missed 57 games last season because of a knee injury, which was the focus of the physical examination. The Croatian forward has three years left on his current deal worth $16 million.
In 25 games last season, he averaged 14 points and 8.4 rebounds for Boston, which finished with a franchise-worst 15-67 record.
